outcome_intro: Ask which customers have roaming computers off, uninstalled or not checking in, and get one row per customer. Cisco Umbrella plus your AI agent mints a token for each child org in your MSP console and rolls up deployment health, instead of switching into one customer at a time. It also gives one verdict for a suspicious domain and reconciles a block list against your own file.

instead_of_say.instead: Switch into each customer's dashboard in the MSP console and read down its roaming computers, virtual appliances and tunnels
instead_of_say.say: Which customers have roaming computers off, uninstalled or not checking in this week?

instead_of_say.instead: Look a domain up in Investigate, then search every destination list for it, then run an activity report to see who resolved it
instead_of_say.say: Is login.example.com blocked, what does Umbrella say about it, and who hit it in the last day?

instead_of_say.instead: Compare a destination list with your blocklist file by hand and add or remove entries in the portal one at a time
instead_of_say.say: What would change if I made destination list 1234567 match my blocklist file?

pain_points: In an Umbrella MSP or Multi-org console, deployment status lives inside each child org: Cisco's own description is that the console lists every child org so you can "switch in and out between customers" (Cisco partner blog, December 2022). A fleet-wide health check is one customer at a time.

Answering "is this domain blocked for this client, and who hit it?" means three places: Investigate for the category and risk score, every destination list (including parent-domain entries) for membership, and an activity report for who resolved it.
Keeping a destination list in step with a blocklist you maintain elsewhere is a manual diff, and an allow-list entry that has since been categorized as malicious stays allowed until someone notices.

outcomes.question: Which customers have roaming computers off, uninstalled, stale or without web protection, and how many seats each?
In one customer, which roaming computers, virtual appliances, tunnels and networks have a deployment problem?
For a domain from a ticket: its category, risk score, security status, which of our lists block or allow it, and who resolved it?
Which allow-list entries are now categorized as malicious, conflict with a block-list entry, or were added this week?
What would I add and remove to make a destination list match my blocklist file?
For one customer's QBR: request summary, top threat types and blocked categories against the prior 30 days, and deployment status?

different_vs_wrappers: This skill covers the whole current Umbrella v2 API and is built for the MSP console: it mints a token per child org (X-Umbrella-OrgId) and keeps each customer's synced data in its own local store, so a fleet rollup or an offline search is one command. Existing integrations, such as MSPbots' Cisco Umbrella MCP server and the Splunk and XSOAR add-ons, cover a slice of the API (activity reports, or destination-list edits) one call at a time.
different_vs_vendor: The Umbrella dashboard and MSP console stay your place for policy design and centralized reports; this skill answers the cross-customer and multi-step questions (fleet health, a domain verdict, a list diff) in the AI agent you already use, and complements the console rather than replacing it.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Cisco Umbrella MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Cisco Umbrella data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Does it work with an MSP or Multi-org console?
faqs.a: Yes. Create the API key in the parent console. Every command takes --org <child org ID> (or CISCO_UMBRELLA_ORG_ID) and mints a token for that customer with the X-Umbrella-OrgId header; fleet health walks every managed customer for you. The child token stays in memory and each customer's synced data goes to its own local store.

faqs.q: Which API key scopes does it need?
faqs.a: Only the scopes for what you run: Reports for activity, report-card and verdict's resolver lookup, Deployments for networks, roaming computers and fleet health, which also needs the Admin customers scope, Policies for destination lists, Investigate for categorization and risk scores, Admin for keys and users. A section the key cannot reach returns 403 and is skipped with a note where the command says so; read-only keys cannot change anything.

faqs.q: Will this hit the Umbrella API rate limits?
faqs.a: It is built to stay inside them. Token requests are limited to 20 a minute, so fleet health starts customers 3 seconds apart; narrow a large fleet with --customers or --max-customers. Sync once and search, hygiene and analytics answer from the local store without new API calls.

governance_summary: The skill reads Umbrella deployments, policies, destination lists, reports, Investigate data and MSP customer records, and keeps a local store for offline questions; credential values are withheld from its output and never kept in the SQLite store; the key, secret and bearer token are saved to an owner-only, unencrypted credentials.toml until auth logout. It can also create, change and delete networks, sites, destination lists, tunnels, users and customer records, and it can change API keys and set tunnel credentials you chose. It refuses five actions, because Umbrella returns a new secret only once and this program withholds it: api-keys create, api-keys refresh, s3-bucket-keys, tunnels add with no secret of your own and tunnels update-credentials with auto-rotate or no secret of your own. Do those in the Umbrella dashboard. Let an agent read freely, preview routine writes with --dry-run, and keep a human approving deletes and anything that changes a credential.
